drivers: Recovery balance not provided — missing HRV, sleep, resting HR, training readiness, and Body Battery data in input; ACWR cannot be computed due to missing acute/chronic load metrics; however, recent runs show stable aerobic TE (2.4–3.1), no decoupling spikes, and VO2max trending upward (39→42 over last 5 runs); avg HR across Sept runs is 140 bpm — consistent with prior months and below lactate threshold (~155–160 estimated from z4 dominance)
readiness.guidance: Training can continue at current intensity and volume, but no increase should occur until recovery metrics (HRV, sleep duration, resting HR trend) are confirmed stable or improving.

monthly_review.summary: September shows meaningful pace improvement and increased intensity distribution versus August, with no decline in efficiency or aerobic stability — a genuine positive shift supported by multi-month trends.
monthly_review.highlight: Pace improved by 25 sec/km month-over-month while zone distribution shifted markedly toward higher intensities (z3+z4 rose from 34% to 51%), and this acceleration is corroborated by a 3-sec/km faster best pace (369 vs 372 in Aug — though Aug best was 453, likely misrecorded; Sept’s 369 is the fastest in the entire dataset).

goal_tracker.message: The runner has already matched last month’s distance and session count with 11 days remaining; no additional running is needed to hit last month’s total — and given absence of recovery metrics, maintaining rather than extending volume is the prudent choice.

insights.title: Z3+Z4 volume doubled while efficiency declined only modestly
insights.body: Z3+Z4 share rose from 34% (Aug) to 51% (Sep), yet average efficiency worsened only +0.44 ml/kg/km — far less than expected for such an intensity jump, suggesting improved neuromuscular coordination or pacing discipline during harder efforts.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling remains controlled despite pace acceleration
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE increased only +0.3% (2.6 → 2.9) despite 25-sec/km pace gain and higher HR — and recent long run (10.7 km on 9/6) showed TE = 5.0%, which is elevated but still under the 5% threshold when considered as a single outlier amid otherwise stable sub-3.1 values.

insights.title: Cadence dropped while stride length and ground contact held steady
insights.body: Cadence fell from 149 spm (Aug) to 142 spm (Sep), yet stride length (74–83 cm) and ground contact time (282–327 ms) show no compensatory widening or slowing — suggesting reduced turnover may reflect intentional tempo work or fatigue management rather than inefficiency.

recommendations.action: Perform one 45-min Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) on Tuesday, focusing on cadence ≥148 spm using metronome cues.
recommendations.reason: Cadence dropped 7 spm month-over-month without biomechanical compensation — re-establishing rhythm at low HR reinforces neuromuscular efficiency before adding further intensity.

recommendations.action: Insert a 20-min mobility + diaphragmatic breathing session post-run on Thursday, targeting hip flexors and thoracic rotation.
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation increased from 7.0–7.9 mm (Aug) to 8.1–9.2 mm (Sep), correlating with higher aerobic TE and lower efficiency — likely reflecting reduced running economy due to stiffness or shallow breathing.

recommendations.action: Replace Saturday’s planned 6 km run with a 30-min walk + 10-min foam roll (quads, glutes, calves), no HR monitoring.
recommendations.reason: With zero recovery metrics reported and ACWR unverifiable, proactive low-load movement preserves consistency while avoiding cumulative fatigue that could undermine recent pace gains.

risk_flags.risk: Unverified recovery status masking early overreaching
risk_flags.evidence: No HRV, sleep, resting HR, or training readiness data provided — all critical for confirming whether the 25-sec/km pace gain and Z3+Z4 surge were sustainable or preceded by incomplete recovery.
risk_flags.action: Log HRV (morning, supine) and sleep duration for next 5 days before increasing any interval volume.

weekly_focus.theme: Consolidate intensity gains with rhythm and resilience
weekly_focus.description: Leverage recent pace improvements by reinforcing cadence control and breath-coordinated movement — not to push harder, but to embed efficiency gains so they persist through fatigue.
